task_1.title: Restore for-loop variable name reuse in iterator expressions
task_1.description: Version 2.9.2 fixes a template rendering regression introduced in 2.9.1 where a Jinja `{% for %}` loop could fail if the loop target reused the same variable name that was needed to resolve the iterable expression. The fix restores correct scoping so the iterable is resolved from the pre-loop context before the loop target binding is applied, including async iteration paths.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Jinja templates can render `{% for %}` loops when the loop target uses the same variable name as the object referenced to obtain the iterable, without failing during loop setup or iteration.

expectation.grounded: When `Template.render` evaluates a `{% for %}` statement, the iterable expression must be resolved against the surrounding template context before the loop target binding is introduced. Reusing the same identifier on both sides of the loop, such as using the loop target name inside the iterable expression, must remain valid and must not trigger runtime local-variable or unbound-variable failures. This behavior should hold for normal iteration and the async iteration path.
expectation.conceptual: For-loop variable names should be safely reusable in templates. If a template iterates over data derived from a variable and uses that same name as the loop item, rendering should still work and the loop should consume the intended source data instead of failing because of a scoping regression.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve existing `{% for %}` semantics for templates that already render correctly, while preventing the loop target binding from interfering with evaluation of the iterable expression. It must avoid introducing new runtime errors in synchronous or asynchronous loop execution.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be narrowly scoped to restoring correct loop-variable resolution, without changing normal loop behavior or creating new rendering regressions in other templates.

behavior: A `{% for %}` loop may reuse the same identifier for the loop target and for resolving the iterable source from the current context.
The iterable expression is evaluated using the pre-loop context rather than a context where the loop target has already shadowed the original value.
Rendering such loops no longer fails with runtime errors caused by premature local binding of the loop variable.
The corrected scoping applies in both standard and async iteration flows.
acceptance_criteria: When a template renders a loop such as `{% for widget in widget.subwidgets %}`, it should iterate over the outer `widget.subwidgets` value and render successfully.
When the loop target name is reused inside the iterable expression, rendering should not fail before or during iteration because the target name shadows the original source value too early.
When the same template is rendered through an async-capable environment, the loop should preserve the same correct name-resolution behavior.
When templates use distinct names for loop targets and iterable sources, their existing rendering behavior should remain unchanged.

task_2.title: Restore backward-compatible macro caller handling
task_2.description: Jinja2 2.9.2 restores compatibility for templates that explicitly declare an optional `caller` macro parameter, a pattern used in existing integrations. The update keeps valid call-block behavior working while rejecting invalid or ambiguous `caller` definitions and invocations that would otherwise produce broken or duplicated bindings.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2.9.2 preserves existing templates that explicitly declare `caller` as an optional macro parameter, while preventing ambiguous `caller` signatures or invocations from compiling or executing with duplicate special-caller bindings.

expectation.grounded: When a macro or call block body uses the special `caller` value, the macro may explicitly declare a `caller` argument only if that argument has a default value. In that case, macro invocation must continue to support call-block `caller` semantics without introducing duplicate `caller` parameters. If `caller` is declared without a default in a macro that relies on special `caller` behavior, template compilation should fail. If runtime invocation provides both an explicitly bound `caller` and an additional special `caller` input, the macro should raise `TypeError`. Explicitly declared `kwargs` or `varargs` parameters should not be reintroduced as implicit special capture parameters.
expectation.conceptual: Templates using older but common macro patterns should keep working after the upgrade when `caller` is defined as an optional parameter. Valid direct macro calls and valid call blocks should behave normally, while invalid `caller` declarations or conflicting `caller` inputs should fail clearly instead of compiling into broken functions or silently accepting ambiguous behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not change normal macro behavior for call blocks that omit an explicit `caller` parameter. Only allow explicit `caller` compatibility when the macro signature provides a default for `caller`. Do not create duplicate implicit special parameters for explicitly declared `caller`, `kwargs`, or `varargs`, and do not treat a duplicate `caller` input as a generic extra keyword argument.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing macro and call-block behavior stable except for the targeted compatibility fix. Support the optional-`caller` pattern without broadening ambiguous argument binding, and surface conflicting `caller` usage as a clear failure.

behavior: Macros whose body uses `caller` can explicitly declare `caller` only when it is optional through a default value.
Macros using that optional `caller` pattern should compile and execute without generating duplicate internal `caller` bindings.
Macros that declare `caller` without a default while also relying on special `caller` semantics should fail during template compilation.
If a macro invocation supplies `caller` through both explicit argument binding and special caller handling, execution should raise `TypeError` for the duplicate `caller` value.
Explicitly declared `kwargs` and `varargs` parameter names should be respected as declared arguments instead of being duplicated as implicit special captures.
acceptance_criteria: When a template defines a macro that uses `caller` and declares `caller` with a default value, it should compile successfully.
When that macro is invoked directly or through a call block, it should bind `caller` only once and render according to the provided explicit value or call-block caller.
When a macro uses special `caller` behavior but declares `caller` without a default value, template compilation should fail.
When an invocation would provide two `caller` values to the same macro, it should raise `TypeError` instead of accepting the call.
When a macro explicitly declares `kwargs` or `varargs`, it should not receive duplicated special parameter bindings for those names.
